references.text: Moses went up the mountain to receive the law from God, parallel to how Jesus went up the mountain to teach.
Moses went up Mount Sinai, as a parallel to Jesus' ascent on the mountain to teach.
The book of Psalms speaks of the blessing of following God's ways, which can be seen as a precursor to Jesus' teaching in the Sermon on the Mount.
Jeremiah's prophecies about a new covenant can be seen as related to Jesus' teaching on the mountain, as part of the introduction of this new covenant.
The book of Hebrews refers to Jeremiah and the new covenant, which can be linked to Jesus' teaching in the Sermon on the Mount.
Jesus' transfiguration on the mountain, showing his divinity and authority, strengthens his teaching in the Sermon on the Mount.
